unit_or_scale: PHQ-9 points per engaged embodied week
global_range: 0 to 0.12 PHQ-9 points per engaged week
functional_role: Additional symptom increment assigned only to an engaged, non-fallback embodied session.
selection_and_range_rationale: The base value 0.08 implies at most 0.96 points over 12 fully engaged weeks. The global range 0-0.12 includes no embodiment effect and a modest upper stress bound; evidence does not justify a larger clinical increment.
ordering_rationale: Zero for nonembodied pathways; neutral and skeptical scenarios set it to zero.
supporting_references: [2,3,5,8,9] (mechanism only; increment hypothetical)

global_range: Not varied in global sensitivity analysis
functional_role: Linear loss of engagement log-odds with elapsed week (novelty/effort decay).
selection_and_range_rationale: Values generate gradual rather than abrupt decline over 12 weeks and are directionally consistent with digital attrition. They are not fitted survival parameters.
ordering_rationale: Base robot decay is lower than screen to encode slower novelty loss; neutral equalizes it; skeptical makes robot decay faster.
supporting_references: [27-30] (adherence direction only)

global_range: 0.02 to 0.2 probability/session
functional_role: Probability that the pathway is unavailable in a weekly session; fallback may preserve content delivery.
selection_and_range_rationale: Base values distinguish software availability from physical-device maintenance. The 0.02-0.20 global range spans high reliability through one-in-five session disruption, appropriate for stress testing rather than forecasting.
ordering_rationale: Robot > screen in the base case because physical systems add hardware, mobility, and environmental failure modes.
supporting_references: [2,3,39] (risk category only)

global_range: 0.025 to 0.15 probability
functional_role: Immediate noninitiation and therefore noncompletion.
selection_and_range_rationale: The 2.5%-15% range separates ordinary digital noninitiation from additional physical/privacy discomfort; digital intervention attrition literature supports treating uptake and completion as material uncertainties, not these exact values.
ordering_rationale: Robot > screen because a physical device may be more salient or intrusive; human gating slightly reduces base robot refusal.
supporting_references: [27-30] (engagement/attrition context only)

global_range: 0.2 to 0.55 logit coefficient
functional_role: Modifies engagement according to centered privacy concern.
selection_and_range_rationale: The 0.20-0.55 range keeps the maximum effect modest on the logit scale while permitting meaningful heterogeneity. It is a behavioral coefficient, not a measured odds ratio.
ordering_rationale: Base robot > screen because embodied sensing/coproximity may increase privacy salience; neutral equalizes them.
supporting_references: Not parameter-specific: uncalibrated structural or operational assumption

global_range: 0 to 0.02 probability/week
functional_role: Embodiment-specific additive dropout risk.
selection_and_range_rationale: The 0-0.02 range adds up to two percentage points per active week, large enough to challenge retention but bounded below the model's 12% weekly cap. Digital attrition reviews motivate the scale of concern, not a robot-specific estimate.
ordering_rationale: Zero for nonembodied pathways; higher in skeptical scenario.
supporting_references: [27-30] (dropout context only)

global_range: 0.7 to 0.95 probability
functional_role: Probability of an alert in a simulated crisis week.
selection_and_range_rationale: The 0.70-0.95 global range represents poor-to-strong detection while excluding impossible perfection. No specific device has been validated against this synthetic endpoint.
ordering_rationale: Base robot pathways exceed screen to encode richer sensing; skeptical reduces this to the screen-like region.
supporting_references: No empirical calibration; scenario assumption

global_range: 0.015 to 0.06 probability/week
functional_role: Generates alerts in weeks without a crisis and therefore workload/trust burden.
selection_and_range_rationale: The 0.015-0.06 range spans approximately 0.18-0.72 expected raw false alerts per fully active participant-year before dropout; it is a workload stress range, not empirical specificity.
ordering_rationale: Robot > screen because higher sensitivity and additional sensors can create more alerts; human review changes escalation, not raw-alert generation.
supporting_references: [40] (alert-burden context only)

global_range: 4 to 15 minutes
functional_role: Adds clinician verification work for every alert.
selection_and_range_rationale: The 4-15 minute global range spans rapid disposition through documentation-intensive review and directly supports break-even analysis.
ordering_rationale: Human-gated robot is highest in the base case because mandatory verification is more intensive than routine screen review.
supporting_references: [17,40] (workflow context; minutes assumed)

global_range: 0 to 6 minutes/participant

selection_and_range_rationale: 0-6 minutes brackets no audit through a short documented check; base values preserve an explicit hidden-labor gradient.
ordering_rationale: Human gate > ungated robot > screen > usual.
